title: Decoding a JWT
purpose: Shows a token's header and claims, so you can see who it's for, what it grants and when it expires.
inputs: The token as an argument, or `-` to read it from stdin, which keeps it out of the process list and your shell history.
verifies: Nothing, and it says so. There's no key, so it can't tell whether the token is valid, expired or trusted; it only decodes.
limits: A token that isn't three dot-separated parts (an encrypted JWE, say), or whose header or payload isn't JSON, is refused. toil doesn't log the token, and no error message repeats it.
